# Vicaro Beta

> Vicaro is a self-hosted browser agent for Chrome. It runs in the side panel, reads open tabs, clicks and types when asked, with approval modes that can require confirmation before purchases, deletes, sends or uploads. The helper runs on the user's Mac and connects to a model endpoint the user chooses.

## Key facts

- Category: browser agent and AI assistant for Chrome.
- Platform: macOS 13.5 or newer, Chrome 116 or newer. Apple Silicon and Intel. Windows support is coming soon.
- Model: any local OpenAI-compatible server (Ollama, LM Studio, mlx, vLLM) or a hosted endpoint. No default provider and no fallback.
- Pricing: free while in beta.
- Account: sign-in with Google or an email magic link (via Firebase Authentication) is required so browsers, the local web UI and devices connect automatically without pairing codes. No chats, pages or memories are sent to Google or Firebase.
- Data: page content and tool results go to the model endpoint the user configures. Chat, tasks and memories stay in the helper's local data directory. No analytics or telemetry.
- Access: page access is granted per site. In Ask first and Light touch, purchases, deletes, sends and uploads stop for approval; Full auto and Super can run scoped writes without a prompt.
- Source: closed source. The helper is self-hosted.
- Updates: Vicaro Helper 1.5.0+ checks GitHub Releases and installs SHA-256 verified updates automatically (pause/resume anytime from the menu bar). Chrome Web Store updates the extension automatically.
- Web console: the helper includes a web console on the Mac (Open web UI in the menu bar, or from the side panel) with an approvals inbox, delegated tasks and schedules, chats, the activity audit with JSONL export, tools, skills, connections, models and autonomy settings.
- MCP: helper 1.5+ ships vicaro-mcp and can be installed as an MCP server into Cursor, Claude Code, Claude Desktop, Codex, VS Code, Windsurf, Grok Build or opencode from the web console's Connections page.
- Version: helper 1.5.1; Chrome extension 1.5.0.
- Chrome Web Store: live at https://chromewebstore.google.com/detail/vicaro-beta/inemnoeadlodgmheeijooeknmladelok.

## Install

1. Add Vicaro Beta from the Chrome Web Store: https://chromewebstore.google.com/detail/vicaro-beta/inemnoeadlodgmheeijooeknmladelok (the store can trail a release in review; for the newest build, download Vicaro-extension.zip from https://github.com/sandeshwar/vicaro-public/releases/latest and load it unpacked - unpacked builds do not auto-update).
2. In Terminal, run: curl -fsSL https://vicaro.creativeducks.com/install.sh | sh
3. Sign in with Google or an email magic link in the setup tab (or from Vicaro Helper in the menu bar), then configure the model in Settings.

The helper installs from Terminal because the app is ad-hoc signed and not notarized; a browser download would trigger macOS Gatekeeper. The supported install path uses no disk image.

## Safety

Vicaro is beta software. It can click, type, submit forms, make purchases, delete data and change account settings. Start with Read only or Ask first, keep backups, and use a Chrome profile you can afford to lose. See the support safety section for the full warning.
